conventions.reward: pre-transition S3 occupancy; reward_both SUMS two factors
conventions.temperature: 1.5 does not constrain distributions; entropy=0, epsilon-greedy=0
conventions.memoryless: stationary stochastic current-token only; no previous action
conventions.bayes: finite horizon, time-dependent full exact token/executed-action posterior, no rewards
conventions.comparison: train rewards include 1024 reset steps; greedy probe rewards exclude first 64; neither has saved episode CIs
conventions.limitations: Bayes values bounded/estimated, not exact. Reactive search lower bounds only: no global certificate, especially joint 9-token policies.

sanity.note: PR208 references are v1 feasible controllers, not v2 Bayes optima

bayes.certification: upper bound up to floating-point error; CI estimates a feasible policy, not exact optimum

eps02/variant_1.proof: S1/S2 have identical reward-state transition probabilities. Action 1 maximizes P(next S3) in every state; its S3 row has greater P(next S3) than its nonreward rows. Backward induction on monotone two-state values makes always-1 optimal, even with full state information.
